newsitem.title: INDIA: Profit-takers force Bombay shares to close lower.
newsitem.headline: Profit-takers force Bombay shares to close lower.

text.p: Shares at Bombay exchanges ended with small losses in sluggish trade on Friday, as profit-taking snapped the market's six-day rally, traders said.
"Basically, we saw speculators offloading long positions," said Manish Nathwani, dealer at brokers Samir Doshi. "Quite a lot of stocks had been in overbought zones."
The market showed a downward trend from opening levels, but heavy selling near close on the last day of the weekly trade account pulled prices, traders said.
Bombay's benchmark 30-share index ended nearly one percent lower at 3,836.07, off 3,878.99 -- the intra-day high.
"The reaction was expected to be lower on the last day of end-account trade, but the market showed some strength," said Kuntal Shah, chief dealer at local brokers D.T. Gandhi.
A market correction was widely anticipated due to profit-taking, but prices could resume an uptrend after a bout of profit-taking, participants said.
Foreign funds were buyers in shares of term-lender Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) which saw a price-limit set on the stock, dealers said.
ICICI rose 4.50 rupees or 6.3 percent to end at 75.25, but off 77.75 -- the day's high in volumes of 1.69 million shares.
Shares of Southern Petrochemicals Industrial Corporation ended 1.50 rupees, or ten percent, up at 18.75 after the firm announced its 1996/97 (April-March) results.
The company said its 1996/97 net profit dropped marginally to 726.2 million rupees from 811.1 million in the year-ago period. The firm maintained dividend at three rupees a share.

The market is now watching for a long-pending hike in petroleum product prices expected to be announced by the ruling United Front's policy-setting committee on June 15 to tackle a soaring oil subsidy bill.
